name: Jizhao
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Shao Lanzhu 2016 (documentation of Jizhao, endangered mainland Be/Tai-Kadai language; Chinese-language study cited on Glottolog)

readall_conflicts: No stress statement was obtained from any source, so there is no disagreement about stress. There is a genetic-classification disagreement between the two listed authors: Li Jian 2011 (abstract) treats 吉兆海话 as a Putian-Min (Chinese) dialect island with Zhuang admixture, while Li Jinfang & Wu Yan 2017/2022 treat 吉兆话 as a non-Chinese Tai-Kadai language closest to Be/Lingao. Both describe the same village variety.

sources.note: Reports 6 tones [21, 31, 32, 33, 55, 45] from Shao 2016:15 and implosives /ɓ ɗ/ from Li & Wu 2017; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: 李锦芳、吴艳 (Li Jinfang & Wu Yan). 2022. 论吉兆话的系属地位 [On the genetic position of the Jizhao language]. 民族语文 Minzu Yuwen 2022(6): 11-25.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Section 二(一) 声调演变特点 (p. 14) gives the tone system in comparison with Proto-Tai and Lingao/Be (4 unchecked tones, 3 checked tones, D1 split 55 vs 33 by vowel length); a full-text search for stress/accent the full scanned for 重音/轻重/轻音/重读 finds no occurrence. Comparative-classification paper, not a phonological description.
